# Fixtures where the SELF-HOST arm64 path disagrees with the native compiler.
#
# Format: <fixture-name> <#issue> <reason>
#
# Same contract as selfhost-wasm-known-divergences.txt: TestFernFixturesSelfHostArm64
# lists these rather than skipping them, so the lane is green with them listed, a
# NEW divergence fails, and a listed fixture that starts PASSING also fails — an
# allowlist nobody prunes is where bugs go to be forgotten.
#
# Two rules for adding a row, both learned from the wasm leg's first run (which
# reported 26 mismatches, 14 of them harness artifacts):
#
#   1. Reproduce it by hand with a native self-host CLI (`make selfhost-cli`,
#      ~1.3s per program) before writing it down, and record the measured
#      self-host and native values in the reason.
#   2. Rule out the harness's `import "core/int"` injection first. The native
#      legs inject that import into the entry file (LoadCheckMono, for wasmbin's
#      PrintMainResult); the self-host CLI injects nothing. A compile failure
#      naming a missing method is that asymmetry, not a compiler divergence.
#
# This leg's failures come from TWO layers, and the reason should say which:
# `-target arm64` emits AND assembles AND links in-process (asm_arm64_ir +
# arm64_native + elf.fern), so a compile failure is either an emitter bail
# ("module is not IR-eligible") or the in-process assembler refusing an
# instruction it does not implement (the message names the mnemonic).
#
# Measured 2026-08-04 on the run that closed #6045: 317 fixtures run, 302 pass,
# 15 listed. Two of those 15 — `tuple_match_expr` (#6010) and `multiline_stdin`
# (#6052) — were fixed within hours of this leg landing and were pruned in
# #6099, `pure_collection_aliases` + `map_struct_value_field` with the #6007
# slices, `derive_json` with #6009, the six regex fixtures with #6049, and
# `map_struct_enum_keys` with #6081, `url_codec` with #6082,
# `audit_io_builtins` with #6083 and `generic_method_typeparams` with #6007,
# leaving NONE. Every row was reproduced by hand
# with bin/fern-selfhost and checked against BOTH `bin/fern -interp` and the
# self-host x86-64 path, which is what split the list into its two halves:
#
#   * Rows the x86-64 leg lists too, with the SAME measured value. Those are
#     shared frontend/irlower bugs that arm64 merely re-observes; fixing one
#     flips two legs. Keep the issue numbers in sync with
#     selfhost-x86_64-known-divergences.txt — this happened TWICE during review:
#     #6080 fixed eq_struct_enum + ord_struct_enum, and #6085 fixed int_wrap
#     (#6050) + u64_max_to_f64_is_huge (#6051), on both legs. Each time the leg
#     reported "listed but PASSES now" before anyone thought to re-check, which
#     is the contract earning its keep — four rows that would otherwise have
#     sat here as permanent expected failures.
#
#     It has now happened FOUR times, and the last two were not caught by
#     review at all: #6088 (tuple_match_expr / #6010) and #6094 (multiline_stdin
#     / #6052) both branched BEFORE this leg existed, so their authors pruned
#     the wasm and x86-64 files — the only two that existed when they started —
#     and never saw this one. The stale rows only surface on the NEXT pull
#     request, since the workflow is `pull_request`-only and nothing runs the
#     leg on a push to main. So: when a shared-frontend fix prunes a row, prune
#     it from ALL THREE files, and re-read this file rather than the one your
#     branch was cut against.
#   * NO rows left that pass on x86-64 AND interp and fail only here. The
#     arm64-specific frontier (#6081 / #6082 / #6083) is closed.
#
# The list is now EMPTY: no assembler-refusal row survives (every "hit an
# instruction it does not yet support" failure is gone), and the last compile
# row — the shared #6007 IR-eligibility bail — went with the generic-struct
# method-type-param fold. Keep the contract in force rather than deleting the
# file: an empty allowlist is what makes the NEXT divergence fail the leg.
#
# #6081 (`map_struct_enum_keys`) was one of those arm64-only rows and is now
# fixed: the arm64 map runtime had no keyed-compare path at all, so a struct /
# enum key fell through to the STRING loop and `__fern_str_eq` read the key box
# ({shape-ptr, field0, …}) as a `{data, len}` string box — comparing field 0 as
# a LENGTH and then walking the shared shape pointer. Two keys therefore matched
# iff their first field was bit-identical. A `Name { first: string, … }` key
# missed (two distinct string-box pointers), which is what the fixture saw; a
# scalar-only struct key would instead have OVER-matched on any key with the
# same field 0. That second half is pinned by TestSelfHostMapKeyedArm64IR, since
# no fixture probed it.
#
# #6082 (`url_codec`) was the other, and its filed diagnosis was wrong in an
# instructive way: it read as a `Url` struct / Option payload laid out at the
# wrong offset. It was neither. The in-process GAS parser stripped `//` line
# comments with a plain `indexof(line, "//")`, blind to string quoting, and the
# emitter escapes `"` / `\` / control bytes but not `/` — so `.ascii
# "http://h.com"` was truncated to `.ascii "http:`, shortening that literal and
# shifting every constant after it in .rodata. Any arm64 program with `//`
# INSIDE a string literal was affected; url_codec was simply the first fixture
# to contain one. Pinned by TestSelfHostArm64GasStringComment.
#
# #6083 (`audit_io_builtins`) was the last, and like #6082 it was an assembler
# hole rather than a codegen one. `__fern_eprint_str` claimed its newline
# scratch with `strb w1, [sp, #-16]!`, a pre-index WRITEBACK the assembler has
# no byte-store encoder for: it dropped the `!`, left sp unchanged, and the
# paired `add sp, sp, #16` then RAISED sp by 16. eprint's own output was
# correct, so the frame corruption only surfaced at the next call — which is
# why the fixture printed "Hi!"/"to-stderr" and died afterwards. The helper now
# uses __fern_putchar's explicit `sub sp` shape, and the assembler REFUSES a
# writeback form it cannot encode (`<mnem>:writeback`) instead of silently
# dropping it. Pinned by TestSelfHostArm64GasWriteback.

# --- shared with the x86-64 leg (same bug, same measured value) ---

# --- arm64-self-host only (passes on interp AND the self-host x86-64 leg) ---

# --- negative literals (#6394) ---------------------------------------------
# The native compiler accepts the smallest i32 as a literal, and negative
# literals as match patterns; the self-host lowers neither, so both bail to a
# strict-IR refusal rather than producing a wrong answer.
#
# `smallest_int_literal`: `return -2147483648;` bails with "`return` of unary
# `-`". Narrow to the boundary magnitude — `return -5;`, `return 0 - 5;` and
# `var v: i32 = -5; return v;` all lower. The magnitude is out of i32 range as
# a POSITIVE value and the return-of-unary gate judges it without the sign,
# which is the shape the native checker had before it threaded a `negated` bit
# through settleInt.
#
# `negative_literal_patterns`: the whole `match` bails. The self-host parser's
# literal-pattern test looks at one token and the sign is a separate one, so
# `-1 => …` is declined — again the shape the native parser had.
smallest_int_literal 6394 self-host: `return -<literal at the i32 limit>` does not lower
negative_literal_patterns 6394 self-host: negative literal patterns do not lower

# --- i32 arithmetic through a negated literal (#6396) ----------------------
# `int_min_arithmetic`: `var a: i32 = -2147483648;` is accepted by the
# self-host and then computed in 64 BITS — the annotation is ignored, and
# `0 - a` reads 2147483648 where every native backend reads -2147483648.
# Not a bail: it compiles and answers wrong. The same value written
# `0 - 2147483647 - 1` is correct, so the two spellings of one number
# disagree. Ordinary i32 overflow (`2147483647 + 1`, `* 2`) wraps correctly,
# so truncation is not missing in general — `a` is simply not an i32.
int_min_arithmetic 6396 self-host: a negated out-of-i32-magnitude literal widens to 64 bits

# --- array-element reclaim through .with (#6397) ---------------------------
# `struct_field_array_with_reclaim`: the native side of this leak is FIXED
# (the field release was a buffer-only free that dropped no elements); the
# self-host leaks all THREE shapes the case measures, including the bare
# local one native has always handled — 88 / 31 / 32 bytes per round against
# native's flat. So this is the self-host's own reclaim gap rather than the
# same bug, and it needs the RECLAIM side of the Perceus port rather than the
# one-line release fix native took.
struct_field_array_with_reclaim 6397 self-host: .with does not reclaim the replaced element, in any of the three shapes
